verdict.text: Fully self-serve. You can create an OAuth app and have real users connect in minutes, with no review.
verdict.label: Sourced

quick_setup_checklist.text: Go to GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → **New OAuth App**.
quick_setup_checklist.label: Sourced
quick_setup_checklist.note: Sourced; upgrade to Tested if you did this in your lab

hands_on_time.label: Inferred
hands_on_time.note: Tested only if you timed it | converted to Inferred: guide-spec section 2 says a time estimate is never Tested unless someone waited it out

composio_status.text: Toolkit available, with a Composio managed app. Bring-your-own is optional, used for your own branding on the consent screen.
composio_status.label: Sourced
composio_status.note: Sourced: Composio docs; Tested if you saw both consent screens

prerequisites.text: A homepage URL for your app (any valid URL works)
prerequisites.label: Sourced

prerequisites.text: The callback URL from Composio's dashboard if you're using Composio
prerequisites.label: Sourced

setup_steps.text: Start here: On GitHub, go to Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App.
setup_steps.label: Tested

setup_steps.text: Fill in the application name and homepage URL. While testing, any valid URL works, such as your portfolio or GitHub profile; GitHub doesn’t verify it.
setup_steps.label: Tested

setup_steps.text: Click Register application and copy the Client ID.
setup_steps.label: Tested

setup_steps.text: Click Generate a new client secret and copy it immediately, since it’s shown only once.
setup_steps.label: Tested
setup_steps.note: Tested, if you saw it disappear after leaving the page; otherwise Sourced

setup_steps.text: In Composio, go to Toolkits and select GitHub. GitHub appears as two toolkits: choose the GitHub card (OAuth2, marked “Managed”), not GitHub MCP, which uses an API key and skips OAuth entirely.
setup_steps.label: Tested

setup_steps.text: Create the auth config with your own credentials: keep the default config name or give your own, paste the Client ID and Secret, then click Create Auth Config.
setup_steps.label: Tested

setup_steps.text: Copy the callback URL Composio shows and paste it into your GitHub OAuth app’s “Authorization callback URL” field, then save on GitHub.
setup_steps.label: Tested
setup_steps.note: Tested, if you did this; adjust the order to match what you actually did

setup_steps.text: In Composio, go to Auth Configs → select your GitHub config → Connect Account. You’re redirected to GitHub’s own login page, where you sign in with your GitHub username/email and password.
setup_steps.label: Tested

setup_steps.text: On GitHub’s consent screen, confirm it shows your OAuth app’s name, check the requested permissions, and click Authorize.
setup_steps.label: Tested

scopes.text: Request only what you need, e.g. `read:user`, `repo` (full repo access) or `public_repo`. Scopes are chosen at authorization time, not in the app settings.
scopes.label: Sourced

limits_before_approval.text: None; there's no approval step for OAuth apps.
limits_before_approval.label: Sourced

approval_process.text: None for using the app. Listing on GitHub Marketplace is optional and has its own review.
approval_process.label: Sourced

likely_blockers.text: **Organisation restrictions:** If a user's organisation restricts third-party OAuth apps, an org owner must approve your app before it can access org repos. Users may connect successfully but see no org data.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced
likely_blockers.note: Sourced; this is a great "gotcha" to verify if you have an org

likely_blockers.text: **One callback URL per OAuth app**, so you may need separate apps for development and production.
likely_blockers.label: Sourced

likely_blockers.text: **GitHub Apps vs OAuth Apps:** GitHub generally recommends GitHub Apps for finer permissions. Check which type Composio's custom auth expects.
likely_blockers.label: Uncertain
